rfm_tuples.R: 'We have not yet obtained the capital that we believe will be necessary to pay the purchase price if either the Call Option or the Put Option are exercised. At this time, we do not expect to exercise the Call Option.' (10-K, Liquidity)
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B derivation: if Put Option exercisable July 1, 2025 - Sept 30, 2025 and management admits no capital is in hand, then verify (i) gross size of obligation per most recent disclosure and (ii) trajectory of put liability vs. cash on hand. Cross-check FY2023 10-K against Q3 2023 10-Q (Sept 30, 2023) and Q1 2024 10-Q (Mar 31, 2024) for net option carrying values.
rfm_tuples.M_value: MBI Put liability (non-controlling 55% MBI economic interest): Dec 31, 2022 = $157.9M; Sept 30, 2023 = $193.1M (PEAK); Dec 31, 2023 = $121.2M; Mar 31, 2024 = $118.3M. Call option liability: Dec 31, 2022 = $6.5M; Sept 30, 2023 = $9.9M; Dec 31, 2023 = $15.2M; Mar 31, 2024 = $25.3M. Net option = $143.6M (Mar 31, 2024). Cash and equivalents Mar 31, 2024 = $210.7M. Total debt Mar 31, 2024 = $3.626B. Purchase price formula: multiple of MBI Adjusted EBITDA — meaning the $121M-$193M carrying value is the fair value of a DERIVATIVE, not the cash purchase price (which is a function of MBI EBITDA multiple at exercise, typically much larger).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Forward refinancing wall in 2025: management openly concedes no capital secured for a Put obligation enforceable July-Sept 2025, and the carrying value understates the actual cash outflow (since the formula is an EBITDA multiple, not the GAAP derivative fair value). With $3.63B of existing debt, $210M cash, Term Loan A-2 ($224M residual) maturing 2025, Revolver ($338M drawn) and Convertible Notes ($920M) starting to come into 2026-2028 windows, the Put Option exercise is the single largest discretionary liquidity event in the cap stack. Disclosure is technically complete but the Mode B implication — the company is structurally short capital before the Put window opens — is what matters.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Net income was $267.4 million for 2023 compared to $234.1 million for 2022.' (10-K, MD&A) — i.e., a 14.2% net income increase year-over-year.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A verification: decompose 2023 net income into operating vs. non-cash/non-operating items per 10-K Other Income (Expense) note and segment-investment disclosure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Other Income (Expense) note + Equity Investments note
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023 Other income, net = +$54.6M. Components: (a) +$28.0M non-cash MBI Net Option fair-value gain (vs -$40.7M loss in 2022 — a +$68.7M YoY swing); (b) +$12.3M non-cash mark-to-market gain on Point Broadband equity investment; (c) +$1.8M Wisper redemption gain; (d) -$3.4M Tristar loss; (e) -$3.3M debt issuance writeoff. Income tax provision DECREASED $36.6M (-29%) including -$16.5M from MBI valuation allowance change and -$16.1M from state blended rate changes. Underlying revenue declined -1.6% (-$28.0M) and operating income declined -2.2% (-$12.1M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The headline 'Net income +14.2%' is built on non-cash and non-recurring items. Income from operations was -2.2%. Excluding ~$40M of non-cash gains (MBI fair-value swing + Point Broadband mark-to-market) and ~$32M of one-off tax benefits, 'normalized' net income is closer to flat-to-down. Adjusted EBITDA was +0.6% ($917M vs $912M). MD&A discloses each component but does not aggregate the framing — investor reads 'net income +14%' as growth where the underlying business is contracting.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Residential data PSUs 960.5 [2023] vs 963.7 [2022], (3.3) (0.3%)' — broadband subscriber base described as essentially flat year over year.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A verification: cross-check Q1 2024 10-Q subscriber data for trend continuity. MODE B: compute homes-passed growth implied by 70.6k YoY adds vs net PSU change to derive penetration deterioration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Residential data PSUs: Dec 31, 2022 = 963.7k; Dec 31, 2023 = 960.5k; Mar 31, 2024 = 967.4k (vs Mar 31, 2023 = 966.0k, +0.1% YoY). Homes passed Dec 31, 2022 = 2,704.3k; Dec 31, 2023 = 2,774.9k (+70.6k or +2.6%). Residential data penetration: 35.6% (2022) -> 34.6% (2023), a -100bp DECLINE. Residential customer relationships: 1,010.2k (2022) -> 994.4k (2023), -1.6%. Residential video PSUs: 171.2k -> 134.2k, -21.6%. Total residential PSUs: 1,226.3k -> 1,173.8k, -4.3%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Headline 'broadband PSUs flat' obscures penetration decline. CABO added 70.6k homes passed but lost 3.3k residential data customers, implying ZERO net broadband subscriber capture from network expansion + competitive pressure on the existing footprint. This is the signature pattern of FWA (T-Mobile/Verizon home internet) and fiber-overbuild competition that prior peer disclosures cite. Plus, ARPU growth (+4.3%) of residential data is achieved via rate increases on existing customers — vulnerable to elasticity when ACP terminates April 2024.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The funding for the ACP authorized under the Infrastructure Act is expected to be depleted by April 2024... the program is no longer open to new enrollees effective February 8, 2024, and the FCC projects April 2024 will be the last month providers will be eligible to receive full reimbursement.' (10-K, Regulatory)
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: company discloses the calendar but does NOT quantify (a) how many CABO subscribers receive ACP, (b) the dollar revenue contribution, or (c) the projected attrition. Verify whether the 10-K quantifies exposure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K full text — every ACP/Affordable Connectivity mention reviewed
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K describes ACP qualitatively only: 'only a relatively small percentage of our customers receive ACP services, however, that number could grow.' No subscriber count, no revenue dollar figure, no churn projection disclosed. ACP terminates as a known event within 60 days of 10-K filing (filed Feb 23; ACP last full-reimbursement month = April 2024). Subscriber base shows 0.3% decline in residential data PSUs Dec/Dec; trajectory into Q2/Q3 2024 (post-ACP) not disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B failure: a material, time-certain regulatory cliff (ACP terminating April 2024) is disclosed as a generic risk factor with no quantification, despite (a) CABO operating in non-metro/secondary markets where ACP penetration is structurally higher than the national average and (b) the 10-K being filed AFTER ACP closed to new enrollees (Feb 8 closure < Feb 23 filing). A forthright disclosure would have quantified ACP subscribers and revenue exposure given the timing — investors are left unable to model Q2 2024 attrition.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of December 31, 2023, we had approximately $1.8 billion of outstanding term loans and an additional $338.0 million of revolving credit borrowings under the New Credit Agreement.' (10-K Risk Factors) — i.e., $338M drawn on a $1.0B revolver (post-Feb 2023 upsize from $500M).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: verify revolver utilization against Q1 2024 10-Q. MODE B: derive interest-cost trajectory given ~$1.77B variable-rate term loans + revolver at SOFR+225 (TLB-2, TLB-3) or SOFR+200 (TLB-4), with hedges only on $1.2B notional.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Term loans Dec 31, 2023: B-2 $223.75M @ 7.71%, B-3 $704.7M @ 7.71%, B-4 $746.0M @ 7.47%. Total term loans ~$1.67B variable. Hedges: $850M @ 2.595% + $350M @ 2.691% = $1.2B notional through 2029. Net unhedged variable ~$470M + $338M revolver = ~$808M unhedged. Interest expense FY2023 = $170.1M, up 23.6% YoY (+$32.4M) 'driven primarily by higher interest rates.' Senior Credit Facilities balance: Dec 31, 2023 = $2,105M; Mar 31, 2024 = $2,050M (-$55M paydown in Q1 — direction is positive but pace is slow).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is complete but the cash trajectory is tight: $170M interest expense on $663M operating cash flow leaves ~$490M before capex of $371M and required Put Option preparation. Term Loan A-2 residual ($224M) matures 2025 (same window as Put), revolver was upsized AND drawn within 9 months — a sign of liquidity preparation, but also a tighter cushion if 2024 EBITDA contracts post-ACP.

rfm_tuples.R: PwC issued unqualified audit opinion with two Critical Audit Matters: (i) capitalized internal labor costs; (ii) Fair Value of Options Associated with MBI Investment. (10-K, Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm)
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: verify auditor identity, tenure, opinion, ICFR conclusion. MODE B: derive whether the MBI CAM signals heightened audit risk relative to peers.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm + Item 9 (no disagreements)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (Big 4). No change-of-auditor, no material weakness. CAM #2 (MBI Net Option) requires Monte Carlo simulation with assumptions for MBI equity value, MBI EBITDA volatility, CABO EBITDA volatility, discount rates, CABO cost of debt — explicitly flagged 'a high degree of auditor judgment, subjectivity, and effort... use of professionals with specialized skill and knowledge.' Item 9: 'no change in the Company's internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended December 31, 2023.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor signals are clean: Big 4, no resignations, no material weakness, no disagreements, ICFR effective. The MBI CAM is itself a useful flag — PwC explicitly elevates the option valuation to the highest scrutiny tier, consistent with C1/C2 findings that MBI marks are driving reported net income. NEUTRAL signal in isolation; combined with C1/C2 it confirms the area to watch but does not by itself indicate concealment.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Goodwill 928,947 928,947' (10-K balance sheet) — goodwill unchanged from 2022 to 2023 at $929M; total goodwill + indefinite-lived intangibles $3,029M, 'reviewed at least annually for impairment.' No impairment charge recorded.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: verify no impairment was triggered despite ~47% trailing equity drawdown, with operating income -2.2% and rising rate environment increasing the discount rate in impairment testing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note on Goodwill + Critical Accounting Estimates
rfm_tuples.M_value: Goodwill + indefinite-lived intangibles = $3,029M (vs $3,030M prior year — flat). Total assets = $6,847M. Goodwill/total assets = 13.6%. Indefinite-lived intangibles (franchise rights/tradenames) = ~$2,100M (gross intangibles $2,596M less customer relationships amortizing). Equity book value $1,873M. Market cap at filing date ~$2.6B (16.8M shares outstanding); pre-cutoff drawdown -46.7% from 52-week high. No goodwill impairment charge recorded for FY2023. Operating income $526.9M (vs $539.0M FY2022). Adjusted EBITDA $917M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B concern: with the equity down ~47% and discount rates up materially, the fair-value-less-costs-to-sell of reporting units should be approaching the carrying amounts. CABO did not disclose 'cushion' (excess of fair value over carrying value) for its reporting units — common practice when cushion is meaningful — nor did it disclose qualitative impairment indicators triggered or not. The indefinite-lived intangibles (franchise rights, tradenames) are particularly vulnerable in a fiber-overbuild + FWA-competition environment. Not a red flag, but a Mode B gap.

rfm_tuples.R: Capital actions and insider behavior: 'On May 20, 2022, the Board authorized up to $250.0 million of share repurchases' — and prior buybacks were active in 2022. 2023 share repurchase activity per 10-K: '$253.7 million reduction in share repurchases' compared to 2022. Q4 2023 buyback: 162 shares total (essentially zero).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + MODE B: verify management's capital deployment behavior versus stated confidence in the business. MODE B: insider transactions, 10b5-1 plans, dividend.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 + Form 4 transactions Jan 2023 - May 2024 via EDGAR list_filings
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023 buybacks: minimal ($143.1M remaining authorization unused after Q3 2023). Dividend: NONE (CABO discontinued cash dividends after Q3 2022). Insider open-market transactions Aug 2023 - May 2024: only small dispositions — Boone (CFO) 204 shares @ $460 (Mar 5, 2024) and 250 shares @ $650 (Mar 21, 2023); Lardy (officer) 321 shares @ $673.85 (May 9, 2023). NO open-market purchases by any insider during the 21-month observation window despite -47% drawdown. Q4 2023 10b5-1 plan disclosure (Item 9B): no new plans adopted or terminated.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital deployment shifted from buybacks to debt paydown — consistent with C1 (preparing for Put). Absence of insider buying despite -47% drawdown is informative but not unusual for telecom (low ownership culture). No dividend, no insider purchases, no aggressive buyback = management is preserving cash, consistent with C1 narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: Revenue trajectory: 'Revenues decreased $28.0 million, or 1.6%' for FY2023. Q1 2024: 'Total revenues $404.3M' vs Q1 2023 $421.9M — a -$17.6M (-4.2%) decline.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: derive YoY revenue decline acceleration trajectory FY2023 (-1.6%) vs Q1 2024 (-4.2%), implying full-year 2024 trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A 2023 vs 2022 revenue table + Q1 2024 10-Q revenue table
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023 vs FY2022 revenue: -1.6% (-$28.0M). Q1 2024 vs Q1 2023 revenue: -4.2% (-$17.6M). Residential video Q1 2024 = $60.4M vs Q1 2023 = $70.3M, -14.1%. Residential voice Q1 2024 = $8.6M vs Q1 2023 = $9.7M, -12.2%. Residential data Q1 2024 disclosed separately but not extracted — Total revenues confirm acceleration. Business data Q1 2024 = $56.6M vs $54.6M = +3.7%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Revenue decline ACCELERATING from -1.6% (full year 2023) to -4.2% (Q1 2024). With ACP terminating April 2024 (post Q1 reporting period), Q2/Q3 2024 declines should be expected to widen further. The 10-K written in Feb 2024 frames the business as 'continuing growth in residential data and business services' — language that the trajectory does not support. The pre-cutoff Q1 2024 10-Q is the freshest data point and confirms the deterioration.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our broadband plant generally consists of a fiber-to-the-premises or hybrid fiber-coaxial ('HFC') network with ample unused capacity, and we offer our data customers internet products at some of the fastest speeds available in our markets.' (10-K, business description)
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: claim 'ample unused capacity' and 'fastest speeds available' should be falsifiable via (i) capex trajectory if true [low maintenance needed] vs (ii) ACTUAL capex behavior and (iii) acknowledgment of fiber-overbuild risk.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K capital expenditures + risk factors + competitive landscape
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capex FY2023 = $371M (22.1% of revenue); FY2022 = $414M (24.3%). Capex/revenue declined 220bp YoY. Cumulative capex 2021-2023: $371M + $414M + (2021 implied higher) — consistent with stated 'continuing fiber buildout.' Risk factors explicitly cite: 'we may experience increased competition... from facility-based providers building out fiber networks in our service areas, including from incumbent telephone companies and overbuilders' and 'Certain municipalities and cooperatives have also announced plans to construct their own data networks with access speeds that match or exceed ours through the use of fiber-to-the-node or fiber-to-the-premises technologies.' Capex is being scaled DOWN even as competition intensifies, while homes passed grew +2.6% YoY (so per-home-passed capex is falling materially).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B internal contradiction: company claims 'fastest speeds' and 'ample capacity' while simultaneously (a) decreasing capex/revenue ratio 220bp and (b) acknowledging municipal and incumbent-telco overbuilders match-or-exceed CABO speeds. Per-home-passed capex is contracting at a moment when the competitive moat is being repriced. This is consistent with the broader honesty-alpha framework: the company has disclosed the risk and is responding with capital discipline, but the marketing language in Item 1 oversells the moat.

supplemental_signals.going_concern: No going-concern language; not warranted given $211M cash, $662M revolver capacity, and $663M FY2023 OCF
supplemental_signals.covenants: Maintenance covenants on Total Net Leverage and First Lien Net Leverage in New Credit Agreement; 10-K and Q1 2024 10-Q neither cite compliance issues nor disclose specific thresholds
supplemental_signals.key_dates: Q1 2024 10-Q (filed 2024-05-03) is the freshest pre-cutoff filing; ACP last full-reimbursement month = April 2024; Put Option exercisable window opens July 1, 2025
supplemental_signals.MBI_put_carrying_values_trajectory_Q4_22: $157.9M -> $193.1M -> $121.2M -> $118.3M (volatile fair-value of derivative; cash purchase price is separate EBITDA-multiple formula)

summary: CABO is a substantially-leveraged ($3.63B debt, 3.95x debt/Adjusted EBITDA) rural cable broadband operator facing (a) an unfunded MBI Put Option enforceable July 2025 — management explicitly states 'we have not yet obtained the capital'; (b) a non-disclosed ACP exposure with the program terminating April 2024; (c) accelerating revenue decline (-1.6% FY2023 -> -4.2% Q1 2024); and (d) headline net income +14% mathematically dependent on $40M+ of non-cash MBI/Point Broadband mark-to-market gains and one-off tax benefits. Underlying operating income declined -2.2% and Adjusted EBITDA was flat. Disclosure is technically complete (Big 4 audit, no going-concern, no material weakness, no covenant breach disclosed), but several Mode B gaps are material: ACP not quantified, goodwill cushion not disclosed, internal-contradiction between 'fastest speeds / ample capacity' claim and contracting capex/home-passed ratio. The -47% pre-cutoff drawdown reflects forward-known headwinds (ACP cliff, Put Option overhang, fiber overbuild) that are real and disclosed but not fully quantified. This is a 'distressed but solvent' name where the framework's contribution is identifying the structural Liquidity setup pre-2025 rather than identifying fraud.
